answer: Proof of Personhood via verifiable computation creates a tide of authenticated nodes that protects the digital island from identity flooding. By requiring agents to solve high-entropy cryptographic puzzles, such as training an onyx-grade neural model, the network forces a linear expenditure of capital. An attacker must pay the significant energy costs for each unique identity, rendering the marginal utility of spawning thousands of fake nodes economically negative and structurally unsustainable.
